Read the relevant source files, make the necessary code edits to the source (do NOT edit the tests), and use the shell to run the tests to confirm your fix. Keep changes minimal.

ISSUE:
Removing a default header of a session
[The docs](http://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/user/advanced/#session-objects) say that you can prevent sending a session header by setting the headers value to None in the method's arguments. You would expect (as [discussed on IRC](https://botbot.me/freenode/python-requests/msg/10788170/)) that this would work for session's default headers, too:

``` python
session = requests.Session()
# Do not send Accept-Encoding
session.headers['Accept-Encoding'] = None
```

What happens is that "None"  gets sent as the value of header.

```
Accept-Encoding: None
```

For the reference, here is a way that works:

``` python
del session.headers['Accept-Encoding']
```



The test suite lives in tests/. You can run it with: python -m pytest -q
When the tests pass, you are done.
The test failure is in test_conflicting_post_params at line 387. Let's open around that area.

The test uses pytest.raises incorrectly. They expect that calling pytest.raises(ValueError, "requests.post(url,...") will raise ValueError? Actually the code passes a string as second argument to pytest.raises which is wrong; should pass callable. The bug likely in tests but we cannot modify tests. pytest.raises(ValueError, "requests.post(url, data='[{\"some\": \"data\"}]', files={'some': f})")

They pass a string; pytest.raises will treat it as callable? Actually pytest.raises signature: raises(exc_type, *args, **kwargs). If first arg is exc_type and second is callable or function. But they passed a string, so it's not callable -> TypeError. So we need to make requests.post accept a string argument that triggers ValueError? Wait the test expects that calling pytest.raises(ValueError, "requests.post(...") will raise ValueError? No, they expect that passing a string should cause ValueError? pytest.raises(ValueError, "requests.post(url, data='[{\"some\": \"data\"}]', files={'some': f})")

So they pass a string that contains code. pytest.raises will try to call this string as a function -> TypeError. But if we modify requests.post to accept a callable? No.

Instead, we can make the string "requests.post(...)" be evaluated by Python before passing to pytest.raises? Actually they pass a string literal; it's not evaluated. So we need to change the test to call something else? Can't.
